newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa looking vulnerable, due lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa looking vulnerable, due lower.

text.p: Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Cocoa still looks vulnerable, with the 1,000 stg a tonne level on benchmark September critical, technical analysts said on Friday.
Traders called it to open four stg lower.
Cocoa was probably going to head down again, Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden said. The recent rally above 1,000 stg had been corrective.

"If 1,000 were to break there could be another 50 drop," he said. "At the moment it looks vulnerable." But if September could head through resistance above 1,063 and clamber above 1,070 the picture would be more positive, he said.
Brokers GNI were also looking for a test of support. "All things considered it is more likely that September will move to test 1,000 stg support in the near future," GNI said.

In New York, heavy long liquidation by speculators sent CSCE cocoa futures sharply lower on Thursday, with the benchmark September contract tumbling nearly three percent to its lowest settlement in five weeks, traders said.

The slide came despite predictions of an increase in U.S. second quarter grindings. Most analysts expected the grind, due out on Friday at 1245 GMT, to rise by five to 10 percent compared with the same year-ago period. Estimates, however, have ranged from a five percent decrease to a 15 percent increase.
"Traders are generally unconcerned with the grind," GNI said.
